doc.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Wynton Marsalis, 'roux' and the Ken Burns series
summary: Davern mocks the 'roux' gumbo remark in Ken Burns's Jazz series and its talking heads.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Now see, I thought I wasn’t going ask about it but—

That’s what I mean, Wynton comes on, “roux.” There’s a chapter in the first one, it’s called R-O-U-X, and it actually says, and there he is, cute as a button you know. “Now you could have all kinds of ingredients, you’re going to make a gumbo see? But you
could have them all in there, but if you don’t have roux, you don’t have gumbo, you have gumbo soup, heh, heh, heh” [scats].

And from then on, every time he got into — well the talking heads kept going around. Isn’t that right Sonny? “Oh indubitably. He held the same intensity of emotions as for Charlie Parker with the exact same amount of platitudes as he did for Louis Armstrong.” He made him sound like he was talking about the same person. Them talking heads.
